claims.summary: Imported Grochow-Pitassi Theorem2.3 (April2014 manuscript): their depth-d modular Frege presentation is polynomially simulated over F_p by depth-(d+2) IPS. The read binary sequent/3CNF proof constructs Hilbert-like certificates and includes Boolean axioms. A matching bounded-depth Hilbert-like IPS size lower bound would suffice for that Frege presentation; no low-PC-degree conclusion follows.
claims.assessment: Established published simulation, attributed to Grochow and Pitassi. Exact statement and Section2.3 proof read; Section1.6 Hilbert-like syzygy-coset framework also read. Presentation conversion, field and hard-input certificate model must be matched. No new simulation, unrestricted IPS lower bound, or solution of the binary goal is asserted.
claims.rationale: Source-backed alternative circuit-size boundary, with its missing certificate-coset lower bound explicit. No independent novelty is claimed.
claims.next_action: Develop a size-sensitive invariant or lower bound for the matching Hilbert-like certificate coset; test robustness to its syzygies before claiming a circuit-to-proof transfer.

claims.summary: Over any field, the normalized binary-bag tables p_(x,y)=[[1,1],[-1,0]] and q_(y,z)=[[0,0],[1,0]] have matching y-marginals(0,1), but no joint table supported within both local nonzero supports. This holds on the acyclic two-bag hypergraph.
claims.assessment: Working elementary all-field support control. Every q-supported joint table is zero at y=0, contradicting p(0,0)=1. It does not refute the positive-real marginal theorem or rule out signed extensions that cancel on forbidden local entries. The support requirement models local allowed choices; field-valued zero marginal can conceal nonzero local weights.
claims.rationale: Route-specific check prevents importing positive marginal gluing into finite-field coefficient supports. No claim of independent novelty or lower-bound progress.
claims.next_action: Require positivity or a separate support-preserving gluing proof in any future marginal-based source interpretation.

relationships: Preserves the earlier field, input complexity and placeholder/multilinearity mismatch warnings; the general simulation does not supply those restricted lower bounds.
